items.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: He brought me Herbie Hancock “Head Hunters,”

ctx.x: Is that right? That’s really weird.

Well it’s absolutely true. And I remember I wrote a piece for two pianos that was on a sort of composer forum concert at the school or whatever. And there were people looking at each other, because everybody was writing sort of atonal music and this thing was very tonal and romantic. And I remember seeing two older composers looking at each other and giggling. And I remember feeling, I just don’t have a place in this world in this music. And then I went to — two things happened at once. I went to a Bob Hope show,…

quickly as I could so that my last year of school all I did was work on my own. I studied with Manfredo Fest, who is a Brazilian pianist that lived in Minneapolis. He was blind but he taught me — all our lessons we just transcribed Bill Evans by ear and it was amazing. And then I tried to write a few things for the big band, and I learned on my own. And I learned from friends that I was in school with that were playing. There was a guy named Dave Slutten who sadly just died, a young guy, but he and I would get…
